Chocolate cake (gâteau au chocolat)

The traditional French grandmother's chocolate cake. Crackly crust, soft inside. Serves 6.

Home page

Ingredients

Cake

  • 200g dark chocolate
  • 120g butter
  • 4 eggs
  • 150g sugar
  • 80g flour
  • 6g baking powder (1/2 sachet)
  • 50g dark chocolate chips
  • Icing sugar (optional, can be replaced by glazing)

Tin

  • 10g soft butter
  • 10g flour

Glazing (optional, replaces icing sugar)

  • 150g dark chocolate
  • 150g heavy cream

Recipe

Preparation

  1. Preheat oven to 180C before anything else.
  2. Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over a pan of simmering water. Stir until fully melted, then keep stirring a little off the heat to cool it down. Too hot, it would cook the eggs.
  3. Butter the tin with soft butter, then dust evenly with flour. Put the tin on a baking sheet.
  4. Crack the eggs one at a time into a glass before adding to the bowl, in case one is bad. Add the sugar and beat with an electric mixer until pale and thick (ribbon stage). Doable by hand, it just takes longer.

Mixing

  1. Fold the melted chocolate into the eggs gently but fairly quickly so the mixture does not deflate.
  2. Mix the flour and baking powder with the chocolate chips, then fold in the same way.
  3. Pour into the tin.

Baking

  1. Bake 30-40 minutes at 180C depending on your tin size. Test with a knife blade: if batter sticks, give it 5 more minutes. In a 26cm tin the cake was already cooked at 35 minutes, so check early.
  2. Let it cool a little in the tin before unmoulding. Warm cakes are very soft and fragile.
  3. A well lined tin releases the cake by itself. Otherwise run the tip of a knife around the edge.
  4. Dust with icing sugar, unless you do the glazing.

Glazing (optional)

  1. Prepare the dark chocolate in a heat resistant bowl, in small chips
  2. Pour the heavy cream into a pan and heat it up to boiling
  3. Pour the heavy cream into the chocolate chips
  4. Mix until homegenous
  5. Apply the glaze on the cake. Decorate it if it's for children :)

Notes

This cake looks like a simple grandma cake but is simple and tastes good

The top cracks, that is normal. For a perfectly clean unmoulding, line the tin with baking paper instead. Best eaten warm with whipped cream melting on top.
